_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Based on pterodactyl/game-eggs' tModLoader egg (MIT).
name: tModLoader
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Terraria with mods. Installs the tModLoader release you choose and creates the world on first start; put mods in the mods folder.
startup: read -r need 2>/dev/null < .raptor-dotnet || need=8; if ! dotnet --list-runtimes | grep -q "^Microsoft.NETCore.App $need\."; then echo "This tModLoader version needs .NET $need, which this image doesn't have. Choose .NET $need in Startup, then start the server again."; exit 1; fi; if [ -n "${SERVER_PASSWORD}" ]; then set -- -password "${SERVER_PASSWORD}"; fi; exec dotnet tModLoader.dll -server -ip 0.0.0.0 -port {{SERVER_PORT}} -maxplayers {{MAX_PLAYERS}} -motd "{{MOTD}}" -lang {{LANGUAGE}} -world ~/saves/Worlds/{{WORLD_NAME}}.wld -worldname "{{WORLD_NAME}}" -autocreate {{WORLD_SIZE}} -config serverconfig.txt -savedirectory ~/ -tmlsavedirectory ~/saves -modpath ~/mods "$@"

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# tModLoader. Downloads the release from tModLoader's GitHub releases and
# checks it against GitHub's SHA-256. Worlds (saves/), mods (mods/) and
# serverconfig.txt are never touched; the game's files are only replaced
# once the new release has downloaded and checked out.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server

repo=tModLoader/tModLoader
want="${VERSION:-latest}"
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
build=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
trap 'rm -rf "$build"' EXIT
rm -rf "$build"
mkdir -p "$build"

if [ "$want" = latest ]; then
    tag=$(gh-release tag "$repo" latest) || fail "GitHub can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
else
    tag="v${want#v}"
    case "$tag" in v0.*) fail "tModLoader $tag is for the old Terraria 1.3 and isn't supported. Set Version to latest, or to a 2022 or newer release such as v2026.09.3.1." ;; esac
    gh-release tag "$repo" "$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "tModLoader has no release $tag. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as v2026.09.3.1."
fi
sum=$(gh-release assets "$repo" "$tag" | awk '$1 == "tModLoader.zip" { print $2 }') || fail "GitHub can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
[ -n "$sum" ] || fail "tModLoader $tag has no tModLoader.zip to install."

if [ -f tModLoader.dll ] && [ "$(cat .raptor-tmodloader 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag $sum" ]; then
    echo "tModLoader $tag is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading tModLoader $tag"
    gh-release download "$repo" "$tag" tModLoader.zip "$build/tModLoader.zip" || fail "The download failed. Reinstall to try again."
    mkdir "$build/x"
    # Not its example serverconfig.txt, which would replace yours.
    unzip -q "$build/tModLoader.zip" -d "$build/x" -x serverconfig.txt
    [ -f "$build/x/tModLoader.dll" ] || fail "The download didn't contain tModLoader. Reinstall to try again."
    # Libraries a release dropped would still load, so they're replaced whole.
    rm -rf Libraries
    cp -a "$build/x/." /mnt/server/
    echo "$tag $sum" > .raptor-tmodloader
fi
mkdir -p saves/Worlds mods
[ -f serverconfig.txt ] || printf '# tModLoader settings: https://terraria.wiki.gg/wiki/Server#Server_config_file\ndifficulty=0\n' > serverconfig.txt
# The .NET version it needs, which the startup command checks.
jq -r '.runtimeOptions.framework.version' tModLoader.runtimeconfig.json | cut -d. -f1 > .raptor-dotnet
echo "Installed tModLoader $tag. It needs .NET $(cat .raptor-dotnet)."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The tModLoader release to install, such as v2026.09.3.1, or latest.

variables.name: World name
variables.description: The world's file name in saves/Worlds, created when there's none: letters, digits, - and _.

variables.name: World size
variables.description: The size of a new world: 1 (small), 2 (medium) or 3 (large).

variables.name: Difficulty
variables.description: The difficulty of a new world: 0 (classic), 1 (expert), 2 (master) or 3 (journey).

variables.name: Max players
variables.description: How many players can join at once.

variables.name: Password
variables.description: The password players join with. Empty lets anyone join.

variables.name: Message of the day
variables.description: The message players see when they join.
variables.default_value: Please don't cut the purple trees!

variables.name: Language
variables.description: The server's language: 1 English, 2 German, 3 Italian, 4 French, 5 Spanish, 6 Russian, 7 Chinese, 8 Portuguese, 9 Polish.
